rationale: The centered-product form is internally consistent with the stated congruence story and is motivated by a real sign reversal in the archive, but it forces the long leg to hold both deep-value harvesters and expensive heavy investors — a corner that the archive's own "Expensive Empire Builder Short" and the standard investment/asset-growth literature say should underperform — so the positive expected sign rests on a single pooled two-tail result rather than solid priors.

The expected positive sign asserts that, among the most expensive firms, heavier reinvestment predicts *higher* returns, which directly contradicts the best-established region of the investment/asset-growth anomaly (strongest underperformance precisely among high-multiple, high-capex firms), so the proposal's sign is driven by back-fitting one pooled archive result rather than by a defensible mechanism.

This is an explicitly cosmetic re-encoding of Signal 1 — rank-z instead of winsorized-z on legs already winsorized at 1 sd — and tests a data-handling choice rather than an economic mechanism, which the research objective specifically discourages.

The two-year lag adds genuine economic content (overhang timing plus mitigation of contemporaneous price/capex simultaneity) rather than being a pure re-encoding, though it remains one of five near-identical products in this batch and inherits the questionable glamour-tail sign assumption.

With aqc coalesced to zero for the majority of firm-years, the second leg collapses to a near-constant positive multiplier for non-acquirers, so for most of the cross-section the signal degenerates into plain book-to-market (a rediscovery of the value premium), and the acquirer subsample is longed on the counterfactual premise that expensive serial acquirers outperform.

Double industry z-scoring is a substantive, well-motivated refinement that removes the mechanical capital-intensity sector bet embedded in the raw product and converts the interaction into a genuine within-industry discipline test, even though it still depends on the untested congruence sign in the glamour tail.
